rationale:
bugs_open/283 round 8 — round 7's gating HIGH was CONFIRMED BY CONTROL and is now closed in code; the other three objections are answered with the code lines, an enforced guard, and the verbatim SQL evidence the librarian asked for.

(1) bug_historian HIGH (markup parity excludes script bodies; the payload IS the script) — CONFIRMED before fixing: a rewrite replacing every inline script body with an empty IIFE was run against the 22,791-byte affordability fixture; it retained 58% overall (above the 50% collapse floor) and drew ZERO issues from the judged gate AND the comparative write guard. The seat found a real hole of exactly the class this whole fix exists for. Closed with two comparative checks in JudgedConversionIssues (commit 35d2e0f9c): 5a — prefixed script-reference parity: every {{.InstanceID}}-x token in the BASELINE's inline script bodies (outside comments) must survive into the candidate's, because the brief only ADDS script references (rewired handlers gain lookups; reworked bindings gain the prefix); a dropped reference is deleted logic. 5b — comparative script-mass floor: candidate inline-script bytes >= 0.7 x baseline's; the wrapper only grows a script; the 0.7 is REASONED not measured (no live rewrites exist yet) and is flagged for recalibration at the canary. Regression pair pinned in component_instance_bindings_test.go: the gutted rewrite now refuses on BOTH checks; a rewrite dropping a SINGLE lookup refuses on parity alone; the identity rewrite trips neither.

(2) bug_historian MEDIUM (is compositionHazards blocking or advisory?) — BLOCKING on both paths, at the code: compositionHazards feeds UnprefixedBindings' return (component_instance_bindings.go, appended before the sort); a non-empty UnprefixedBindings makes GateConvertedTemplate return needsJudged=true, which REFUSES the mechanical write (fix arm returns needs_script_scoping, nothing written), and is judged-gate check 4, which refuses the judged write. Live proof it discriminates: tool-fuel-budget-forecaster's JUDGED classification in the 2026-08-19 census comes precisely from its composition hazard ('fg-'+id with both fleetSize and fg-fleetSize declared).

(3) debug_historian MEDIUM (486 double-application poisons newest-first rollback) — accepted and enforced: 486 now opens with a DO block that RAISES when check_scope_route is already present, BEFORE snapshot_agent runs, so a re-apply cannot take a mislabelled pre-image; the ROLLBACK file gains the inverted guard (refuses to 'restore' a row 486 never patched). Same pattern as 487's enforced 486-precondition from this round.

(4) prior_art_librarian MEDIUM + missing items — the verbatim evidence, run 2026-08-19 against the live DB and pods:
  (a) owned-page delivery completions: SELECT count(*) FROM site_work_items w JOIN pages p ON p.name = w.spec->>'page_name' AND p.site_id = w.site_id WHERE w.item_type='section_edit' AND w.status='complete' AND p.rebuild_policy='owned'  ->  19. (tool-improver's own delivery step; the landmine's refusal describes save_page_sections' GENERIC save — the 15 cancelled items of 283 §13.6 — not the targeted section-editor path.)
  (b) backup-before-write: SELECT change_source, count(*) FROM component_versions GROUP BY 1  ->  scope_component_instance = 69 (one pre-image per converted row, taken by the batch before each write); the repair arm takes a NEW pre-image per row under change_source='repair_instance_scope_bindings' inside writeScopedTemplate before any UPDATE.
  (c) deployed-binary liveness: pods run v1.0.1315 digest sha256:1c422c61..., revision 590ca3a20 (label read AFTER digest match), ffef54338 is an ancestor; and the binary itself: grep -ac 'repair_instance_scope_bindings' /proc/1/exe -> 5, absent control grep -ac 'no_such_symbol_283_xyzzy' -> 0. The judged-gate hardening (35d2e0f9c) rides the NEXT roll, and nothing exercises the judged branch until 486 is applied — which stays _HOLD until that roll is digest-verified.

No other edits changed. The plan below is round 7's with the two hardened files updated in place.
